Instance tag *keys* can't contain spaces or\\n `/`, and can't comprise only `.` (one period),\\n `..` (two periods), or `_index`. For more\\n information, see View tags for your EC2 instances using instance metadata.\\n* Tag keys and values are case-sensitive.\\n* The `aws:` prefix is reserved for AWS use. If a tag has a tag key\\n with this prefix, then you can't edit or delete the tag's key or value. Tags\\n with the `aws:` prefix do not count against your tags per resource\\n limit.\\n\\nYou can't terminate, stop, or delete a resource based solely on its tags; you must specify\\nthe resource identifier. For example, to delete snapshots that you tagged with a tag key\\ncalled `DeleteMe`, you must use the `DeleteSnapshots` action with\\nthe resource identifiers of the snapshots, such as `snap-1234567890abcdef0`.\\n\\nWhen you tag public or shared resources, the tags you assign are available only to\\nyour AWS account; no other AWS account will have access to those tags. For tag-based\\naccess control to shared resources, each AWS account must assign its own set of tags to\\ncontrol access to the resource. It is really easy to create some EBS volumes, attach them to your instances, and to store lots and lots of data on them. The same goes for other EC2 resources such as security groups, and EBS snapshots.\\n\\nAs your usage starts to grow from one instance and one application to many instances spanning multiple applications, it can be difficult to track which instances are assigned to which application, which EBS volumes store what data, and so forth.\\n\\nWe\u2019ve just released a very powerful **tagging** feature to allow you to tag your EC2 resources (and also certain shared resources) using up to ten key-value pairs per resource. Each tag consists of a key (up to 128 characters) and a value (up to 256 characters). The tags are stored in the AWS cloud as part of your AWS account, and are private to the account.\\n\\nYou can tag the following types of resources: EC2 instances, Amazon Machine Images (AMIs), EBS volumes, EBS snapshots, and Amazon VPC resources such as VPCs, subnets, connections, and gateways. You can tag existing resources and you can tag new resources right after you create them.\\n\\nYou can manipulate your tags using three new API calls:\\n\\n> **CreateTags** allows you to tag one or more EC2 resources with one or more tags.\\n>\\n> **DescribeTags** gives you the tags associated with one or more resources. The returned tags can be filtered by resource identifier, resource type, key, or value. You can, for example, retrieve all of the tags for a given resource, or you can retrieve all of the resources (regardless of type) with a given tag.\\n>\\n> **DeleteTags** allows you to delete a set of tags from a set of resources.\\n\\nThe existing EC2 \u201cDescribe\u201d APIs (**DescribeInstances**, **DescribeVolumes**, and so forth) return the tags associated with each of the resources in the response.\\n\\nYou can also manipulate them using the EC2 command-line tools (**ec2-create-tags**, **ec2-describe-tags**, and **ec2-delete-tags**) and from the AWS Management Console.\\n\\nYou can create and delete tags using the AWS Management Console. You can view the tags associated\\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/new-amazon-ec2-feature-resource-tagging/\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"EC2: New-EC2Tag Cmdlet | AWS Tools for PowerShell\",\"context\":\"## Description\\n\\nAdds or overwrites only the specified tags for the specified Amazon EC2 resource or resources. When you specify an existing tag key, the value is overwritten with the new value. Each resource can have a maximum of 50 tags. Each tag consists of a key and optional value. Tag keys must be unique per resource.\\nFor more information about tags, see Tag your Amazon EC2 resources in the *Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud User Guide*. For more information about creating IAM policies that control users' access to resources based on tags, see Supported resource-level permissions for Amazon EC2 API actions in the *Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud User Guide*\",\"url\":\"http://docs.aws.amazon.com/powershell/v4/reference/index.html?page=New-EC2Tag.html&tocid=New-EC2Tag\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Checking AWS documentation for EC2 tag limits per resource."}

{"id": "aa5ce387-ffb9-4a31-9812-04223f7fd311", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "You can attach up to **50 tags** per EC2 instance.

A few extra details worth knowing:
- Each tag key must be unique per resource, and can have only one value.
- Max key length is 128 Unicode characters; max value length is 256 Unicode characters.
- Tags with the `aws:` prefix (reserved for AWS use) don't count against that 50-tag limit.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
